entities.summary: Dhia' ul-Dīn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Yūsuf al-Juwaynī al-Shafi'ī was a Persian Sunni scholar famous for being the foremost leading jurisconsult, legal theoretician and Islamic theologian of his time. His name is commonly abbreviated as al-Juwayni; he is also commonly referred to as Imam al-Haramayn meaning "leading master of the two holy cities", that is, Mecca and Medina. He acquired the status of a mujtahid in the field of fiqh and usul al-fiqh. Highly celebrated as one of the most important and influential thinkers in the Shafi'i school of orthodox Sunni jurisprudence, he was considered as the virtual second founder of the Shafi'i school, after its first founder Imam al-Shafi'i.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a leading jurisconsult and legal theoretician of his time, Al-Juwayni's work had significant regional impact on Islamic orthodoxy, shaping the Shafi'i school of Sunni jurisprudence. His influence can be seen in the development of Islamic law and theology for centuries to come.
